thread.title: Slow Start for Dow Despite Merger News, Gain for Oil - Barron's

title: Slow Start for Dow Despite Merger News, Gain for Oil - Barron's
text:
Slow Start for Dow Despite Merger News, Gain for Oil By Updated Jan. 7, 2019 8:03 a.m. ET Order Reprints Illustration by Michael Haddad Text size
Merger Monday: Eli Lilly & Company (ticker: LLY) said it is buying Loxo Oncology (LOXO) for $8 billion. That deal follows on last week’s news that Bristol-Myers Squibb (BMY) was buying Celgene (CELG) in a deal valued at nearly $90 billion. With all the merger activity going on, investors will have a lot to talk about at the 37th annual JP Morgan Healthcare Conference, which kicks off today in San Francisco. In equity markets, Asian stocks rose in overnight trading, but European shares were down. U.S. futures were modestly lower this morning as well. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were flat, S&P 500 futures were 0.1% lower and Nasdaq Composite futures dipped 0.3%. In today’s Morning Movers, we… …visit Las Vegas; …and look for a bottom in oil stocks. Barron’s Briefs CES: The annual consumer-electronics show in Las Vegas is under way. That is where automotive and consumer-electronics firms will try to wow visitors with autonomous driving and artificial intelligence technologies . Sunday, Apple (AAPL) announced a partnership with rival Samsung (005930. Korea). In the future, the iTunes app will be available directly on Samsung smart TVs. It’s a small example of Apple’s strategic shift from selling hardware to generating subscription revenues . Investors have been focused on Apple’s iPhone revenues , which came in light for the fourth quarter. Apple stock has fallen to just 11 times estimated earnings for 2019. American Made: Nucor (NUE) said Monday it would build a new plate mill in the Midwest U.S.. That announcement comes after the release of a Steel Dynamics (STLD) plan to build a new flat-rolled-steel mill , in November. The U.S. is a net importer of steel products, which makes the Trump tariffs and quotas very important for the sector. Steel stocks dropped last year even as steel price rose. It seems that investors don’t yet believe the tariffs will stay in place, but that CEOs do. Oil: Oil was up again Monday morning for the sixth day in a row. Goldman Sachs cut its oil estimates for 2019 Sunday, but the broker’s $55.50 target for U.S. prices is still above the current level of $49 per barrel. Several analyst are looking for a bottom in oil stocks after a difficult 2018, when the energy components of the S&P 500 dropped by more than 20%. This morning, Jefferies upgraded Cabot Oil (COG) and RBC upgraded Continental Resources (CLR) and EOG Resources (EOG). Barron’s continues to like MLP investments . Those are energy stocks, but their performance isn’t necessarily tied to energy prices. As long as U.S. production continues to grow that sector could see gains. Tibor Kárpáti
